schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: path-to-regexp is a runtime dependency and drives the public matcher syntax. v7 and v8 removed the `:param?`, `:param*`, `:param+` and `(regexp)` forms that NEMO documents and users depend on, so a major bump here is a breaking change for consumers, not a chore. Any upgrade needs a deliberate PR with matcher changes, docs and a major release.
Next.js releases get their own PR as soon as they land, rather than waiting for the weekly window — the compatibility matrix verifies them.
React and its types move together.
fumadocs packages are versioned in lockstep and drift between minors.

Linting and formatting tooling, batched — noisy individually. eslint-config-next is excluded on purpose: packageRules are merged in order, so without the exclusion this rule would override the Next.js group set above and split the Next.js packages apart.
Non-major devDependency updates are safe to land on green CI.
Never widen or narrow the published peer range automatically — it defines which Next.js versions consumers may use.
The docs app is not published; keep its churn out of the release notes.
